name: minidlna
desc: Media server software, compliant with DLNA/UPnP-AV clients
why: A DLNA/UPnP-AV media server that is a clean door into the SSDP and UPnP-AV protocols running in most homes.

brief.what_it_is: ReadyMedia, formerly MiniDLNA, is a media server daemon that makes photos, music, and video available to DLNA/UPnP-AV clients such as TVs and media players on a home network. The SourceForge page describes it as "a simple media server software." The Homebrew entry lists its executable as minidlnad, a non-interactive daemon written in C. The page does not spell out its inputs or outputs beyond serving media files to clients.
brief.why_it_exists: The project aims to be "fully compliant with DLNA/UPnP-AV clients." It was originally developed by a NETGEAR employee for the ReadyNAS product line.
brief.install_notes: The SourceForge page lists no install steps and no build instructions. The Homebrew metadata says that to use `brew services`, the configuration should go at ~/.config/minidlna/minidlna.conf. That path comes from the brew caveat, not from the project's own docs. The SourceForge page lists the project as Linux-only.
brief.standout: It is a small, single-purpose daemon that implements the DLNA/UPnP-AV media-server side in plain C. The scout note frames it as an accessible way into the SSDP and UPnP-AV protocols that run in most homes, but the fetched page does not confirm any protocol details.
brief.status: quiet. The SourceForge page shows a last update of 2023-06-02, and the project has been registered there since 2008-10-22. Reviews from 2018 and 2025 are positive, and a 2018 reviewer wrote "Very happy it's still maintained." I found no release or commit data beyond the SourceForge update date.
brief.caveats: The fetched page held only a short description, with no README text, usage docs, or command examples. The reachable docs were thin: the ReadyMedia web site guess at readymedia.sourceforge.io returned HTTP 404. A 2018 reviewer complained "No binaries in the download!!" The page says the project is "not in any way endorsed by the Digital Living Network Alliance®." The license is GPLv2. The Linux-only tag is SourceForge metadata, and I did not check build requirements.
quotes: ReadyMedia (formerly known as MiniDLNA) is a simple media server software, with the aim of being fully compliant with DLNA/UPnP-AV clients.
It was originally developed by a NETGEAR employee for the ReadyNAS product line.
It is not in any way endorsed by the Digital Living Network Alliance®.
fetch_log: https://sourceforge.net/projects/minidlna/ - worked, but the page was mostly site chrome and boilerplate; the project description, license, date, and review data came from it

judge.reason: A lightweight DLNA/UPnP-AV server makes the media-discovery protocols running on home networks tangible, even if its documentation is sparse.

entry.title: minidlna (ReadyMedia)
entry.tldr: A small C daemon that serves your music, photos and video to TVs and media players on the home network, via DLNA/UPnP-AV.
entry.deeper_look:
ReadyMedia, formerly MiniDLNA, is a media server daemon. Point it at folders of music, photos and video, and DLNA/UPnP-AV clients on the same network, such as smart TVs and media players, can find and play them. Its executable is `minidlnad`, a non-interactive daemon written in C. The project describes itself as "a simple media server software, with the aim of being fully compliant with DLNA/UPnP-AV clients."

It began life at NETGEAR: "originally developed by a NETGEAR employee for the ReadyNAS product line." That explains its shape, a small single-purpose service meant to run quietly on a modest box and do one job. The project also states that it is not endorsed by the Digital Living Network Alliance.

The interesting part is what sits underneath. A server like this is a way into how consumer devices discover and talk to each other on a home network: a TV appears to find the server on its own, browses a catalogue, and streams a file. The scout's view is that this makes it a practical door into the UPnP-AV family of protocols. The project page itself does not go into protocol detail, so the specifics are left for you to explore with a packet capture or the UPnP specs.
entry.install:
brew install minidlna
# To use `brew services`, put your configuration at ~/.config/minidlna/minidlna.conf
# Needs DLNA/UPnP-AV clients (a TV or media player) on the same network to be worth running.

try_this.what_happens: Prints the daemon's command-line options, the safest first look since the project page gives no usage examples.

entry.whats_unique: It is a deliberately small, single-purpose C daemon for the server side of DLNA/UPnP-AV, born in a NAS product rather than as a general media centre.
entry.caveats: The SourceForge page is thin, with no README or usage docs, is tagged Linux-only, and was last updated in June 2023.
